milestones.name: Reset to first frame
milestones.summary: Static generation covers all 2273 identities in the compact reset-to-visible corpus, including 15 executable S-CPU WRAM identities decoded from private witnesses. The first-frame runtime executes 254 identities; a clean-BWRAM route-only sweep finds that 24 of a supplied 102-edge NMI schedule reach the post-route inventory checkpoint after 1433720 whole blocks with all 2273 identities dispatched at live S-CPU $00002C / SA-1 $00A6E7 endpoints. The endpoint SA-1 $2209 latch is 0, so S-CPU $2300 remains in its measured wait. The new value-free message summary records 95 writes and 9405 reads with digest 036824b1d673bf63, while the corresponding private Mesen witness records 76 and 8720 with digest c9d5b52ab4d84ff1. The first ordering divergence is event 1567: static sets while Mesen is still polling zero; write streams align through NMI 20, then static advances 19 writes and 684 reads beyond the witness. The full schedule intentionally fails closed with timing_debt when 78 later signals remain; this closes the compact route corpus, not whole-game parity.
milestones.gate: Hardware events and the fixed first-frame checkpoint match.

blockers.summary: The compact reset-to-visible corpus contains 2273 identities and 2440 edges, and static generation covers all 2273. A clean-BWRAM private route sweep reaches its inventory checkpoint after 1433720 whole blocks with 2273/2273 identities dispatched and live S-CPU $00002C / SA-1 $00A6E7 endpoints; final SA-1 $2209 latch state is 0. The static value-free message signature is 95 writes/9405 reads (036824b1d673bf63), while a seeded Mesen boundary witness is 76/8720 (c9d5b52ab4d84ff1). The first divergence is static event 1567, with pre-NMI polling and post-NMI route timing now the active causal-parity blocker. The full 102-edge schedule processes a decisive 24 signals and then fails closed with timing_debt while 78 later signals remain unscheduled; this is not a static-coverage failure.

Cooperative reset/MVN and post-reset SA-1 scheduling reach the first frame; reset-DMA side effects and PPU parity are exact, and CPU/S-CPU/SA-1/DMA counts match. The remaining work is the post-frame CPU/SA-1 upload handshake, one trailing SPC acknowledgement, and ordered digest parity.
